knowledge:
- key_parameters: hdr.structure=Character vector defining metadata fields to extract from FASTA headers ;; delim=Character delimiter separating fields in FASTA headers ;; id.column=Field name in FASTA headers to use as the identifier ;; fw/rev=Positional intervals or FASTA files defining target binding regions relative to 5' and 3' ends ;; mode.directionality=Direction of primers to design ('fw', 'rev', or 'both') ;; settings=A DesignSettings object containing constraints and PCR conditions ;; init.algo=Initialization strategy for primer design ('naive' or 'tree') ;; required.cvg=Desired coverage ratio of templates (default 1; set to 0 to deactivate constraint relaxation) ;; opti.algo=Optimization algorithm ('Greedy' or 'ILP') ;; fw.id=Keyword identifying forward primers in FASTA headers ;; active.constraints=Character vector of constraints to evaluate or filter
- alternatives: openPrimeRui (Shiny app frontend for openPrimeR) ;; MELTING (external tool for melting temperature) ;; ViennaRNA (external tool for secondary structure) ;; OligoArrayAux (external tool for primer efficiency via DECIPHER) ;; MAFFT (external tool for multiple sequence alignments) ;; Pandoc (external tool for PDF reports)
- when_to_use: Use when designing novel multiplex PCR primer sets to maximize template coverage with a minimal number of primers, or when evaluating and comparing existing primer sets for physicochemical constraints and coverage.
- pitfalls: Missing external dependencies (MELTING, ViennaRNA, OligoArrayAux, MAFFT, Pandoc) can limit functionality, though the package remains partially functional ;; Not setting coverage constraints or setting them too loosely is not recommended for designing primers ;; Using the ILP optimization algorithm (opti.algo = 'ILP') has worst-case exponential runtime and is only recommended for small template sets; use 'Greedy' for larger sets ;; Primer directionalities must be correctly annotated in the FASTA file (e.g., using fw.id) when loading existing primers ;; If primers bind outside the target region, specificity will be evaluated as 0% and the specificity constraint will fail.

workflows.name: design_primers
workflows.intent: Design a minimal set of multiplex PCR primers for a set of template sequences under specific physicochemical constraints.
input: leader.fasta (optional FASTA file containing individual binding regions)
workflows.stages: 1. Load template sequences using read_templates() ;; 2. Assign binding regions using assign_binding_regions() ;; 3. Load and customize design settings using read_settings(), constraints(), and conOptions() ;; 4. Design optimal primers using design_primers() ;; 5. Write designed primers to a FASTA file using write_primers()
workflows.code:
fasta.file <- system.file("extdata", "IMGT_data", "templates", "Homo_sapiens_IGH_functional_exon.fasta", package = "openPrimeR")
seq.df.simple <- read_templates(fasta.file)
hdr.structure <- c("ACCESSION", "GROUP", "SPECIES", "FUNCTION")
seq.df <- read_templates(fasta.file, hdr.structure, delim = "|", id.column = "GROUP")
template.df.uni <- assign_binding_regions(seq.df, fw = c(1,50), rev = c(1,40))
l.fasta.file <- system.file("extdata", "IMGT_data", "templates", "Homo_sapiens_IGH_functional_leader.fasta", package = "openPrimeR")
template.df <- assign_binding_regions(seq.df, fw = l.fasta.file, rev = NULL)
settings.xml <- system.file("extdata", "settings", "C_Taq_PCR_high_stringency.xml", package = "openPrimeR")
settings <- read_settings(settings.xml)
cvg_constraints(settings) <- list()
conOptions(settings)$allowed_mismatches <- 3
design.settings <- settings
constraints(design.settings) <- constraints(design.settings)[!grepl("gc_clamp", names(constraints(design.settings)))]
constraints(design.settings)[["primer_length"]] <- c("min" = 25, "max" = 25)
conOptions(design.settings)[["allowed_mismatches"]] <- 0
optimal.primers <- design_primers(template.df[1:2,], mode.directionality = "fw", settings = design.settings)
out.file <- tempfile("my_primers", fileext = ".fasta")
write_primers(optimal.primers$opti, out.file)

workflows.name: analyze_primers
workflows.intent: Evaluate the physicochemical properties, coverage, and constraint fulfillment of an existing primer set against template sequences.
workflows.stages: 1. Load templates and assign binding regions ;; 2. Load existing primers using read_primers() ;; 3. Load settings and evaluate constraints using check_constraints() ;; 4. Update template coverage using update_template_cvg() ;; 5. Compute coverage statistics and ratios using get_cvg_ratio() and get_cvg_stats() ;; 6. Plot coverage and binding regions using plot_template_cvg(), plot_primer_binding_regions(), and plot_primer() ;; 7. Compute optimal primer subsets using subset_primer_set() and plot them using plot_primer_subsets() ;; 8. Visualize constraint fulfillment using plot_constraint_fulfillment() and plot_constraint() ;; 9. Filter primers using filter_primers() ;; 10. Generate a PDF report using create_report()
workflows.code:
primer.location <- system.file("extdata", "IMGT_data", "primers", "IGHV", "Ippolito2012.fasta", package = "openPrimeR")
primer.df <- read_primers(primer.location, fw.id = "_fw")
conOptions(settings)$allowed_other_binding_ratio <- c("max" = 1.0)
constraint.df <- check_constraints(primer.df, template.df, settings, active.constraints = names(constraints(settings)))
template.df <- update_template_cvg(template.df, constraint.df)
as.numeric(get_cvg_ratio(constraint.df, template.df))
cvg.stats <- get_cvg_stats(constraint.df, template.df, for.viewing = TRUE)
plot_template_cvg(constraint.df, template.df)
primer.subsets <- subset_primer_set(constraint.df, template.df)
plot_primer_subsets(primer.subsets, template.df)
my.primer.subset <- primer.subsets[[3]]
original.cvg <- as.character(get_cvg_ratio(constraint.df, template.df, as.char = TRUE))
subset.cvg <- as.character(get_cvg_ratio(my.primer.subset, template.df, as.char = TRUE))
plot_primer_binding_regions(constraint.df, template.df)
plot_primer(constraint.df[1,], template.df[1:10,])
plot_constraint_fulfillment(constraint.df, settings)
plot_constraint(constraint.df, settings, "gc_clamp")
filtered.df <- filter_primers(constraint.df, template.df, settings, active.constraints = c("gc_clamp", "gc_ratio"))
my.file <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
create_report(constraint.df, template.df, my.file, settings, sample.name = "My analysis")

workflows.name: compare_primers
workflows.intent: Compare multiple pre-evaluated primer sets across physicochemical constraints, coverage, and binding regions.
input: primers_set1.csv, primers_set2.csv (CSV files containing pre-evaluated primer sets)
templates_set1.csv, templates_set2.csv (CSV files containing corresponding template sets)
workflows.stages: 1. Load multiple pre-evaluated primer sets using read_primers() ;; 2. Load corresponding template sets using read_templates() ;; 3. Plot constraint fulfillment comparison using plot_constraint_fulfillment() ;; 4. Plot detailed constraint distributions using plot_constraint() ;; 5. Plot binding region comparison using plot_primer_binding_regions()
workflows.code:
primer.xml <- tempfile("my_primers", fileext =".csv")
write_primers(constraint.df, primer.xml, "CSV")
template.xml <- tempfile("my_templates", fileext = ".csv")
write_templates(constraint.df, template.xml, "CSV")
sel.sets <- c("Glas1999", "Rubinstein1998", "Cardona1995", "Persson1991", "Ippolito2012", "Scheid2011")
primer.files <- list.files(path = system.file("extdata", "IMGT_data", "comparison", "primer_sets", "IGH", package = "openPrimeR"), pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE)
primer.data <- read_primers(primer.files)
sel.idx <- which(names(primer.data) %in% sel.sets)
primer.data <- primer.data[sel.idx]
template.files <- rep(system.file("extdata", "IMGT_data", "comparison", "templates", "IGH_templates.csv", package = "openPrimeR"), length(primer.data))
template.data <- read_templates(template.files)
plot_constraint_fulfillment(primer.data, settings, plot.p.vals = FALSE)
plot_constraint(primer.data, settings, active.constraints = c("gc_ratio", "melting_temp_range"))
plot_primer_binding_regions(primer.data, template.data)
